title: Implement Browser Tab Switching Detection and Focus Monitoring

requirements.summary: Create useFocusMonitor hook to track page visibility and window focus events with timestamp recording
acceptanceCriteria: Hook listens to document visibilitychange events
Hook listens to window blur and focus events
Timestamps are recorded for each leave and return event
Hook can be imported and used in any React component

file_operations.description: Create a custom React hook that sets up event listeners for document visibilitychange, window.onblur, and window.onfocus events. Record timestamps using Date.now() whenever the user leaves (blur/hidden) or returns (focus/visible) to the page. Store leave/return timestamps in state arrays and provide them for consumption by components. Include cleanup in useEffect return to remove event listeners on unmount.

requirements.summary: Calculate time away duration and track switching frequency per time window in useFocusMonitor hook
acceptanceCriteria: Duration away is calculated in seconds or milliseconds
Switch count is tracked and reset per time window (e.g., 2 minutes)
Switching frequency (switches per minute) is calculated and exposed

file_operations.description: Add logic to calculate the duration between leave and return timestamps (in milliseconds). Track the number of switches within a rolling 2-minute window by filtering recent switch events. Calculate switching frequency as switches per minute and expose these metrics (timeAway, switchCount, switchesPerMinute) in the hook's return value. Reset or filter out old switches beyond the 2-minute window using timestamp comparisons.

requirements.summary: Implement distraction score calculation based on switching frequency threshold in useFocusMonitor hook
acceptanceCriteria: Distraction score is a numeric value that increases with frequent switching
Threshold of 5 switches in 2 minutes triggers score increase
Score is exposed by the hook for consumption by components

file_operations.description: Add distractionScore state variable (initialized to 0). Whenever the switch count within the 2-minute window exceeds 5, increment the distraction score. Expose the distractionScore in the hook's return value so components can consume and display it. Optionally implement decay logic to reduce the score over time if switching behavior improves.

requirements.summary: Display dismissible warning component when distraction score threshold is exceeded
acceptanceCriteria: Warning component appears when distraction threshold is exceeded
Message is clear and non-intrusive (toast or subtle notification)
Warning can be dismissed by the user
Warning does not block the user interface

file_operations.description: Create a DistractionWarning component that accepts a visible prop and an onDismiss callback. Display a toast-style notification with the message 'Frequent tab switching detected. Try focusing for a few minutes.' when visible is true. Include a dismiss button (X icon) that calls onDismiss to hide the warning. Use Tailwind CSS for non-intrusive positioning (e.g., bottom-right corner) and styling. Ensure the warning does not block user interaction with the main UI.

Import and use the useFocusMonitor hook to access distractionScore. Add state to track whether the DistractionWarning is visible. When distractionScore exceeds a threshold (e.g., 3), set warning visibility to true. Render the DistractionWarning component with visible and onDismiss props. Implement onDismiss handler to hide the warning and optionally reset the flag after a cooldown period.

requirements.summary: Send distraction score and switching statistics to backend via POST request in JSON format
acceptanceCriteria: POST request sends JSON payload with distraction score, switch count, time away, and timestamp
Request is sent after user returns or at regular intervals
Backend actor receives and stores the data
No personal content, keystrokes, or page content is transmitted

file_operations.description: Add logic to send focus monitoring data to the backend by calling the backend actor's recordFocusScore method (which accepts distractionScore, tabSwitchCount, and timeAway as bigint parameters). Use the useActor hook to access the authenticated backend actor. Trigger data transmission after the user returns to the page (on focus/visible event) or at regular intervals (e.g., every 30 seconds) using a timer. Convert numeric values to BigInt before calling the backend method. Ensure no page content, keystrokes, or personal data are included in the payload.

requirements.summary: Add inline code comments to useFocusMonitor hook for clarity and beginner-friendliness
acceptanceCriteria: Each major section of the hook has a descriptive comment
Comments explain why certain logic is implemented (e.g., why thresholds are chosen)
Variable names are clear and self-documenting
Hook is easy to integrate into any component

file_operations.description: Add inline comments throughout the useFocusMonitor hook explaining each section: event listener setup (visibilitychange, blur, focus), timestamp recording logic, duration calculation (subtracting leave from return timestamps), switch counting within the 2-minute rolling window, distraction score increment logic (threshold of 5 switches in 2 minutes), and backend communication (calling recordFocusScore). Include comments explaining design choices such as why 2 minutes is used as the window and why 5 switches is the threshold. Use clear, self-documenting variable names (e.g., leaveTimestamp, returnTimestamp, switchCountInWindow) to improve readability.
